== Notes for Q975 ==

<b>Sylvarachne</b>
<p>("Sylva" for forest, reflecting the arboreal nature of Phasmatodea, and "Arachne" for spinning, symbolizing the intricate web-spinning of Embioptera.)<b>Myth of Sylvarachne:</b>
<p>Long ago, in the time of the <b>Verdant Weave</b>, when the forests of the world stretched unbroken and teemed with life, there lived <b>Sylvarachne</b>, the Forest Weaver. Born of <b>Arborea</b>, the spirit of the living woods, and <b>Fibrellus</b>, the god of threads and binding, Sylvarachne was a being of quiet artistry and endless patience.<b>The Legend of the Eternal Tapestry:</b>
<p>Sylvarachne was tasked by their parents to create the <b>Eternal Tapestry</b>, a work of living art that would preserve the balance of the forest. It was said that the tapestry would be woven from the strands of moonlight, dew, and shadow, and would hang between the trees to unite all creatures of the woods.
<p>1.</p>
<p><b>The Dance of Shadows (Phasmatodea):</b></p>
<p>To gather the strands of shadow, Sylvarachne disguised themselves as a branch, blending into the forest unnoticed. This skill of perfect mimicry allowed them to gather the soft, elusive shadows cast by moonlight. From this act, the <b>Stick Insects</b> emerged, masters of camouflage who live in harmony with the trees.
<p>2.</p>
<p><b>The Loom of Life (Embioptera):</b></p>
<p>To weave the strands into a tapestry, Sylvarachne spun threads of unparalleled strength and delicacy, using their silk to bind the elements together. This weaving birthed the <b>Webspinners</b>, creatures who became architects of intricate webs, crafting shelters that protect their kin.<b>The Legacy of Sylvarachne:</b>
<p>Once the Eternal Tapestry was completed, it was said that Sylvarachne wove themselves into it, becoming one with the forest and imbuing their descendants with their gifts:
<p>• The <b>Phasmatodea</b> carry the essence of shadows and mimicry, blending seamlessly into their surroundings.
<p>• The <b>Embioptera</b> inherited the craft of weaving and the ingenuity to create homes of silk.
<p>The Eternal Tapestry is believed to still exist, hidden deep in the oldest forests. Legends say that those who find it will glimpse the interconnectedness of all life, a reminder of Sylvarachne’s legacy as the ancestor who bound the natural world together.
